nodes.summary: A position $a = (a_0, a_1, a_2, a_3)$ of natural-number pebble counts on the vertices $v_0, v_1, v_2, v_3$ of $C_4$, with indices read modulo $4$, lies in $Y_{aabc}$ when there is an index $i$ with $a_{i+2} \equiv a_i + 2 \pmod 4$ and $a_{i+1} \equiv a_{i-1} + 1 \pmod 4$.

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ and let $k$ be a natural number. In the $(k+1:k)$-pebbling game on $G$, a move removes $k+1$ pebbles from a vertex and adds $k$ pebbles to an adjacent vertex. This is the set of natural numbers $m$ such that every position with $m$ pebbles in total (a number of pebbles on each vertex, summing to $m$) is an N-position, that is, not a P-position.

nodes.summary: Let $a = (a_0, a_1)$ be a position of the $(2:1)$-pebbling game on the complete graph $K_2$, with $a_0$ and $a_1$ pebbles on its two vertices. If $a_0 + a_1$ is even, then $a$ is an N-position (that is, not a P-position) if and only if $a_0 \not\equiv a_1 \pmod 3$. If $a_0 + a_1$ is odd, then $a$ is an N-position if and only if $a_0 \equiv a_1 \pmod 3$.

This is the finite set of distributions reachable from $a$ by one $(k+1:k)$-pebbling move on $G$: for adjacent vertices $i$ and $j$ with $a_i \ge k + 1$, remove $k + 1$ pebbles from $i$ and add $k$ pebbles to $j$.

nodes.title: A $(k+1:k)$-pebbling move

nodes.summary: Let $n, k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $a$ assign $a(x) \in \mathbb{N}$ pebbles to each vertex $x \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $i \ne j$ be vertices with $a(i) \ge k + 1$. Then the pebbling step from $i$ to $j$, which removes $k + 1$ pebbles from $i$ and adds $k$ pebbles to $j$, gives a position $b$ with $\sum_x b(x) + 1 = \sum_x a(x)$.
nodes.title: A pebbling move removes exactly one pebble

nodes.summary: For every simple graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the number $0$ does not belong to the set of totals $m$ such that every $(k+1:k)$-pebbling game on $G$ with $m$ pebbles is an N-game. Indeed, the empty position admits no move, so it is a P-game.
nodes.title: The total zero is never an all-N total
